sources.entry: Checkmate | Uptime and infrastructure monitoring with real-time alerts

summary.one_liner: Checkmate is a self-hosted uptime and infrastructure monitoring app that checks websites and servers and sends alerts, with an optional Go-based agent (Capture) for hardware stats.
summary.what_it_does: Checkmate regularly checks whether servers and websites are reachable and responsive, recording availability, downtime and response times, and raising incidents and real-time alerts when state changes. It supports HTTP (with SSL certificate expiry), ping, port, DNS, Docker, gRPC, WebSocket, game server and JSON query monitors, plus page speed checks. Its optional Capture agent, written in Go and runnable on Linux, Windows, Mac or Raspberry Pi, reports CPU, RAM, disk and temperature data. Docker monitors can connect to a local socket, a remote daemon over mutual TLS, or a Capture agent. Status pages and notifications go to channels such as email, Slack, Discord, PagerDuty, Telegram and Twilio SMS. The reference deployment is a Docker Compose setup that runs the all-in-one Checkmate image alongside MongoDB.
use_cases: incident alerts sent to Slack, Discord or email
how_to_run: Open the app in a browser and set CLIENT_HOST if accessed from another origin
Optionally build locally: docker build -f docker/Dockerfile -t checkmate .
notable: Scales horizontally with dedicated worker nodes sharing check load through MongoDB; README claims production use monitoring 1,600+ servers on one deployment
Optional Capture agent adds CPU, RAM, disk and temperature monitoring
Docker monitors support local socket, mutual-TLS remote daemon, or Capture agent, with optional container log collection
Broad notification support including PagerDuty, Matrix, Rocket.Chat, Microsoft Teams, ntfy and Twilio SMS
Available in many languages with five status page themes
caveats: MongoDB is required and is not embedded in the application image
Infrastructure metrics (CPU, memory, disk, network) need the separate Capture agent
The Helm chart still deploys legacy images pinned at v3.8.1 and has not been migrated to the all-in-one image
Remote Docker TLS monitoring requires an ENCRYPTION_KEY to be set on the server
keywords: check if my website is down
